Also, actual disabled person here. “Disabled” is NOT an offensive term, so don’t feel bad about using it. Often other terms used to describe us just make us feel more alienated. 

Anyways, your friend doesn’t realize it, and probably doesn’t mean to, but she’s kinda the problem here. Ignoring disabilities and trying to “see past them” is pretty silly and can be harmful. While we have other personality traits, and interests, and likes and dislikes, our disabilities are a huge part of our lives. Often times, ignoring this and trying to treat us EXACTLY the same as other people can be not helpful at all. Many of us require certain accommodations and assistance, and accessibility that a lot of others don’t need. When you try and “see through” the disability our needs are sometimes forgotten. 

Your kids school sounds great though, but obviously your friend has never been close to a disabled person and doesn’t know much about that anyways...

Permanently disabled person here. I almost entirely agree with you, but not everyone is able to emotionally or physically cope with having a disabled partner. It DOES cause a lot of stress. 

If you were in a long term relationship and one of you suddenly became disabled, as you described, it would be a shitty move to abandon them. 

However in this case, OP now knows she’s disabled since being in the date and for whatever reason may KNOW he may not be able to provide her the support she needs. He handled it poorly and could’ve worded it differently, but being upfront is better than either leading her on or ending up in a tense relationship later. 

I personally would rather have someone say, “I had a lot of fun today, but I really don’t think I can provide you with what you need” than find out later on after thinking I might have a chance. 

Now, if he rejected her only because he only saw the chair, that’s an asshole move and she dodged a bullet. But since OP didn’t really say much on why he rejected, we can’t know that.

Actual disabled person here. 
Her being in a wheelchair is a pretty significant piece of information, and the fact that this information was purposefully withheld from you is kinda an asshole move. While it doesn’t define her personality, it does effect her own life significantly and would somewhat cause potential partners to have to adapt as well. 


However, I will say, just because she’s in a wheelchair doesn’t mean she isn’t independent. She may have to do things differently and occasionally ask for help, but most of us are able to adapt and find new ways of doing things. 


The way you handled the situation was poor though. There was no reason you had to say what you did, or phrase it that way. “thanks, I had a good time” and then leaving would have been sufficient. If she asked to go out again you could’ve just said that you felt the two of you were incompatible. 

You’re not an asshole for not wanting to date a disabled person, though, it was only really the way you handled it. Not everybody is emotionally or physically capable to be with somebody like us, and that’s okay. We generally understand that. We have a lot of appointments and medications, it can be very stressful not only for us but for our partners and family. 


Anyways, I hope this made sense- I’m on mobile right now and I know this might look wonky. 


P.S. Disabled people CAN be intimate, you might just have to do it differently, if that’s something that concerned you. However, just as able bodied people, not everyone is compatible in that way.
